newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PAY PANEL LEAVES MILITARY FUMING

The chiefs of the Army, Navy and Air Force were expected to meet the Prime Minister to express their dissatisfaction over several recommendations of the Fifth Pay Commission. The three service chiefs have already met the Defence Minister who was said to have been supportive of their misgivings regarding the recommendations. While recommending a drastic cut in manpower in the Army, Navy and Air Force, the pay panel suggested privatisation and corporatisation of the ordinance factories.
The Times Of India
INDIA READY FOR DIALOGUE WITH PAKISTAN

India was prepared to hold talks with Pakistan at the foreign ministers level, the Prime Minister said. He was commenting on the desire expressed by Pakistan's Prime Minister-elect for talks at the ministerial level between the two countries. The Prime Minister said India always wanted peace in the region from the very beginning and has been working in this direction. On the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, he reiterated India would not sign it in its present form in the interest of national security.
The Economic Times
MINISTRY'S SOPS TO BASIC OPERATORS

The Finance Ministry will treat the first year's licence fee, to be paid by prospective basic telecom operators, as part of the initial project cost. The ministry sought to define the components of project cost to enable the telecom firms raise external commercial borrowings up to 50 percent of the project cost. So far there was no clarity on what would constitute the initial project cost for the purpose of raising debt. Financial institutions were also likely to follow the same norm to arrive at the project cost for telecom companies.
BOMBAY BOURSE SEEKS UNFETTERED FORWARD TRADING

The Bombay bourse's (BSE) proposal on badla (forward trading) seeks to remove all restrictions on the revised carry forward system. The revised system was introduced from January 1996 with a number of restrictions. The misuse of efficient trading mechanism has destroyed continuous price formation of scrips. Violent fluctuation are seen in the prices of certain scrips at every settlement. The BSE was of the view that volatility increased in the past two years and large auctions seen in the recent past were the result of misuse of transactional efficiency provided by the screen based trading.
The Pioneer
STEEP HIKE LIKELY TO KEEP RAILWAYS GOING

The government was faced with the unenviable task of effecting a steep hike in freight and passenger fare in the forthcoming railway budget. This was necessary to maintain the economic viability of the Indian Railways. Latest estimates suggested the Railway Ministry would have to mop up revenues in the region of 150-200 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March). A major chunk of this would have to come from freight and passenger fares to narrow the mismatch between operational costs and service charges, railway officials said.
Financial Express
TELECOM PANEL TO PUSH THROUGH WORLDTEL PROPOSAL

The Telecom Commission would push the WorldTel proposal to begin privatisation of basic services in West Bengal, Kerala and eastern Uttar Pradesh. There were no bidders for these circles in the three bidding rounds held so far. WorldTel offered to bring in almost $1 billion into the country. For the three circles, the government needed to raise only 25 percent of the funds, while WorldTel would arrange the balance. WorldTel also proposed to rope in the state-owned Telecom Consultants as the Indian partner.
OPERATIONAL FREEDOM FOR PROFIT-MAKING BANKS

The Finance Ministry took a step towards offering operational freedom to the profitable banks. It convened the first-ever meeting of select bankers for discussing banks' autonomy in personnel and administrative matters. It was attended by the chiefs of eight profit-making state-owned banks, apart from top government officials. The meeting assumed significance as profit making banks have started tapping the capital market.
Business Standard
A.V. BIRLA GROUP NOT TO DIVERSIFY, DILUTE EQUITY NOW

The A.V. Birla group assured foreign and domestic investors that it would not diversify into unrelated, non-core areas in the near future. It also did not propose to dilute equity of its companies. In a series of meetings with foreign and domestic institutional investors, group executives scorched speculations on forays into steel, purified terephthalic acid and sugar-cum-paper. The assurances came in the wake of concerns expressed by investors over the declining earning potentials of the four major group companies owing to the expected dilutions and diversification.
MINIMUM TAX, DOUBLE TAX ON PAYOUTS MAY GO

The government may drop minimum alternative tax (MAT) and withdraw double taxation on dividends in the forthcoming budget. The Prime Minister had recently promised a review of the tax in the budget. The move comes at a time when the committee on income taxes has come out against any move to align the depreciation rates under the Income Tax and Companies Acts. The government may instead adopt a proposal to phase out the exemptions which were used by zero-tax paying companies. The government was reportedly planning to withdraw taxation on dividend income and replace it with some tax on dividends distribution, to be deducted by the company prior to the dividend declaration.
TRADITIONAL ITEMS TO BLAME FOR SLOWDOWN IN EXPORTS GROWTH

The Commerce Ministry's $38 billion export target for the current fiscal is beginning to look increasingly remote. A host of traditional export items including rice, tea, leather, carpets, computer software, gems and jewellery were leading a slowdown in export growth. Exporters blamed an overall decline in global trade combined with certain factors peculiar to the domestic economy for plummeting exports.
The Observer
IFC MAY MOBLISE $30 BLN LOAN FOR INFRASTRUCTURE

The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, plans to fund infrastructure projects worth $30 to $50 billion in India, with an added priority on power, telecom, water and health projects. The corporation expected a 6-7 percent growth in the coming three to four years, the IFC Asia department director said. ----
Business Line
PROPOSALS FOR PRIVATE BANKS TO BE CLEARED

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was expected to clear the proposals of a few promoters to set up commercial banks in the private sector from a shortlist of 12. After putting on hold all the proposals submitted by a host of corporates for over a year, the RBI now planned to issue letters of clearance initially to a handful of companies from this list, after the budget. None of the top industrial houses figured in this list. Industry sources fancied the chances of finance firms and mid-size corporates.
SUGAR OUTPUT SET TO DECLINE

After the previous year's record output of 16.4 million tonnes, sugar production was expected to drop by 1.52 million tonnes. The projected seven percent decline in output during the 1996/97 sugar season was based on the preliminary estimates given by the major sugar producing states. Officials attributed the estimated drop to the delayed start of the crushing season, lower sucrose recovery in the states and diversion of area under sugarcane to wheat. Trends available so far in the current season indicated a cumulative production of 3.5 million tonnes as on January 7, 1997, as against 4.3 million tonnes during the corresponding period (October 1 to January 7) of 1995/96.
HIGHER ADB COMMITMENT LIKELY

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) planned to commit between $800 million to $1.0 billion in lending to finance India's infrastructure and restructuring programmes this year. In 1996 the bank had commited $763 million. ADB's operations in India this year would pay focussed attention on large restructuring programmes including state power utilities in the energy sector, LPG transmission pipeline project for the Gas Authority of India, large loan for housing finance and port development particularly in Madras and Bombay.
